messages.text: King's former horse Point Of Law wins Melbourne Cup

metadata.summary: Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington.
metadata.content: Melbourne Cup: Point Of Law storms to Flemington glory for Ciaron Maher | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Melbourne Cup: Point Of Law storms to Flemington glory for Ciaron Maher Ciaron Maher continued his outstanding recent record in major races, training Point Of Law to Lexus Melbourne Cup glory at Flemington on Tuesday; stablemates Zahrann and Juja Kibo filled the places. Tuesday 3 November 2026 14:11, UK Image: Ethan Brown rides Point Of Law to win the Melbourne Cup (AP Photo/Asanka Brendon Ratnayake) Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington. Seen as a St Leger hope after finishing fourth in the Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot and winning Newmarket's Bahrain Trophy for former trainers John and Thady Gosden, he was bought privately to continue his career in Australia, winning the Geelong Cup on his first outing for new connections. With stablemate Royal Supremacy setting a strong pace for the big-race favourite to aim at, the son of Frankel showed a deadly turn of foot to run down the eventual fifth as Maher trained not only the first three home but also the fifth and sixth in the 'race that stops the nation'. Maher told Australia's Channel Nine : "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but it's got to execute. I certainly didn't know Royal Supremacy was going to lead by that far but there's nothing better than a true staying test. "Point Of Law has just thrived

metadata.summary: The top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 is not Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe, not Erling Haaland or Lamine Yamal. That honour belongs to Donyell Malen. A revelation at Roma, he makes his return to England against Manchester United on Tuesday night.

Adam Bate examines the transformation of the Netherlands international in Italy Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 3 November 2026 10:41, UK Image: Roma forward Donyell Malen is a man transformed since arriving in Serie A The top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 is not Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe, not Erling Haaland or Lamine Yamal. That honour belongs to Donyell Malen. A revelation at Roma, he makes his return to England against Manchester United on Tuesday night. Malen was a popular figure at Aston Villa but even his biggest admirers might not have anticipated all this. Fourteen goals in 18 Serie A games on loan last season certainly suggested that Roma could get the best from him but Malen has gone to another level. messages.text: Hamilton calls for 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Leclerc incident

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton reiterated "something needs to change" after his latest incident with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc cost the Scuderia victory in Mexico; watch Friday's practice sessions in Brazil from 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Tuesday 3 November 2026 06:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle feels Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's squabbling during the Mexico City GP cost them a one-two finish Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given. Leclerc attacked Hamilton around the outside going into Turn 4 but outbraked himself and cut the corner to take the lead, while Hamilton lost out to Red Bull's Max Verstappen after briefly going off track. The stewards gave Leclerc a five-second time penalty which allowed Verstappen to overtake him during the pit stop phase, going on to win the race while Hamilton finished second and Leclerc in fourth.
